title: Aston Villa Submit Formal Bid for Chelsea Outcast Alejandro Garnacho on Loan
excerpt: Villa have tabled a loan bid with a buy clause for the Argentine winger, who scored just once in the Premier League last season, as they seek to replace Morgan Rogers.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Aston Villa has made a loan bid for Chelsea's Alejandro Garnacho with a buy option.
  • Garnacho scored only one Premier League goal in 24 appearances last season.
  • Morgan Rogers' £117 million transfer to Chelsea has prompted Villa's interest in Garnacho.
  • Chelsea values Garnacho between £42.5 million and £50 million for a permanent transfer.
  • Roma has shifted focus to Crysencio Summerville, reducing competition for Garnacho.
Morgan Rogers Transfer Impact
›Rogers transfer to Chelsea worth up to £117 million.
›Villa seeks Garnacho as Rogers' replacement.
›Garnacho's move could enhance Villa's Champions League squad.
Impact of Rogers' transfer on Villa's strategy.
> **"However, the Serie A club pivoted to pursue Crysencio Summerville from West Ham, with Saudi club Al Hilal also now expected to sign the Dutch international."**

Aston Villa have submitted a formal proposal to Chelsea to sign winger Alejandro Garnacho on loan with an option to buy, according to transfer journalist Fabrizio Romano. The bid marks Villa's most significant move yet in the summer transfer window as they look to bolster their attacking options ahead of a Champions League campaign.

Garnacho, 22, endured a difficult first season at Stamford Bridge after his €46.2 million move from Manchester United last summer. The Argentina international managed just one Premier League goal from 24 appearances and was named in only 14 starting lineups, leaving him well down the pecking order under manager Xabi Alonso.

Rogers Exit Opens Door

Villa's interest in Garnacho has accelerated following the agreement to sell Morgan Rogers to Chelsea in a blockbuster deal worth up to £117 million. With Rogers heading to Stamford Bridge, manager Unai Emery has identified Garnacho as a prime candidate to fill the attacking void on the left flank.

Villa are pushing for a season-long loan with a buy clause rather than a permanent transfer, according to talkSPORT, which reported that the deal includes a conditional obligation to buy. Chelsea had initially been reluctant to sanction a temporary departure but have now come around to the idea, with the club publicly acknowledging that discussions about Garnacho's future are underway.

"We have spoken with the sporting directors and there is interest in him from other clubs, let's see how it develops. Hopefully it finishes in the best possible way for all parties."

— Xabi Alonso, Chelsea Manager

Serie A Interest Fades

Roma had been the frontrunners for Garnacho earlier in the window, submitting a loan offer that Chelsea rejected. However, the Serie A club pivoted to pursue Crysencio Summerville from West Ham, with Saudi club Al Hilal also now expected to sign the Dutch international. That shift opened the door for Villa to formalise their approach.

Napoli, Fiorentina, and Milan had also been loosely linked with the winger, according to Football Italia, but a move to Serie A appears increasingly unlikely. Villa's ability to offer Champions League football gives them a significant edge in negotiations with the player's camp.

![Morgan Rogers. Morgan Rogers' £117 million transfer to Chelsea has prompted Villa's interest in Garnacho.](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/2/28/Morgan_Rogers_England_v_Panama_27_June_26-144_%28cropped%29.jpg)

What Chelsea Want

Chelsea have placed an asking price of around £42.5 million on Garnacho for Premier League clubs, with a slightly lower £40 million valuation for clubs outside England. The exact financial terms of Villa's proposal remain unclear, but the club is pushing to get a deal done in the coming days.

Manchester United retain a 10 percent sell-on clause from the original transfer, meaning they stand to benefit from any future permanent sale. Garnacho was allowed to skip the start of Chelsea's pre-season as the club works to resolve his situation, and he was also left out of Argentina's 2026 World Cup squad following his poor domestic campaign.

A Fresh Start Under Emery

Garnacho is reportedly open to making the move to Villa Park, with the opportunity to work under Emery seen as a key factor. The Spanish manager has built a strong reputation for developing wingers and getting the best out of attacking players who need structure and discipline.

Villa are also understood to hold interest in Paris Saint-Germain youngster Ibrahim Mbaye and Chelsea striker Nicolas Jackson, who spent last season on loan at Bayern Munich. However, Garnacho appears to be the priority signing for the left side of attack.

Personal terms discussions are ongoing between Villa, the player, and his representatives. If completed, the move would see Garnacho become the latest piece in Emery's retooled squad as Villa prepare for their second consecutive Champions League campaign.
